title: quest agents --check exits 0 on version-only drift while its own managed-block text says drift exits 6
description:
Reported by lore-cli (2026-09-14), against quest-cli 0.6.0. lore-cli's CLAUDE.md carried "Quest CLI 0.4.0" against an installed 0.6.0 across two minor versions before being caught, because CI's `quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude` reported exit 0 the whole time:

  $ quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude
  message: Quest agent instruction block records Quest CLI 0.4.0; the installed CLI is 0.6.0. Content is otherwise current.
  state: version-only
  EXIT=0

The managed block's own generated text states "current instructions exit 0, while missing, drifted, or malformed managed instructions exit 6" -- a reader who trusts that sentence concludes CI covers version drift, and it does not: `state: version-only` is a third category that exits like "current" but reads like "drifted."

lore-cli's own framing, worth preserving rather than re-deriving: there are two possible fixes with different blast radii, and a real fix must pick one and say which, not touch only one side:
  (a) the EXIT CODE is wrong -- version-only drift should exit 6 like other drift, in which case every repository running this check in CI has a gate that reports drift and passes anyway, invisibly (CI stays green, so nobody looks); or
  (b) the DOCUMENTATION is wrong -- a version-only difference genuinely should not fail a build, in which case this is a wording fix in the block generator, scoped to correct the "missing, drifted, or malformed... exit 6" sentence to carve out version-only drift explicitly.

lore-cli has no view on which answer is correct, but explicitly warns against a fix that adjusts one side without the other, since that leaves the same disagreement for the next reader to re-derive. `state: version-only` reading like a deliberate third category is a hint toward (b), but this task should reach its own conclusion rather than assume it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is made and recorded on which side is wrong (exit code vs. documentation) -- not just fixed, but stated, so a future reader does not re-derive it
quest agents --check --json/--plain and its generated managed-block text agree with each other for the version-only case specifically, not just for current/missing/malformed
bun run check exits 0 including test coverage for the version-only case at whichever exit code is chosen

plan: 1. Verify the prior investigation lead against current source: confirm checkQuestBlockOnly (agent-instructions.ts) is correctly untouched, and that guides.ts + command-help.ts already document version-only correctly.

2. Fix the actual defect: the embedded CI-hint sentence in questAgentInstructionsFor (agent-instructions.ts ~line 59) predates QCLI-228 and never mentions version-only. Add an explicit carve-out so it no longer implies CI catches version drift.

3. Regenerate this repos own CLAUDE.md managed block from the freshly-edited local source (bun run src/cli/main.ts agents --update-instructions --target claude) so tracker-integrity.yml continues to pass.
4. Record a quest decision documenting this as a doc fix (not an exit-code change): version-only stays exit 0 by design per QCLI-228, the embedded sentence was the thing that lied.

5. Add a test in test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts asserting the generated block text explicitly documents the version-only exemption AND cross-checking that behavior against checkQuestAgentInstructions, so a future regression of this exact gap is caught.
6. Run bun run check end-to-end until fully green.
implementationNotes: Verified the prior investigation lead against current source: checkQuestBlockOnly (agent-instructions.ts) correctly implements QCLI-228's version-only exemption unchanged; guides.ts workspace guide (line ~302-307) and command-help.ts's agents entry already documented version-only correctly when QCLI-228 landed. The ONLY stale artifact was the embedded CI-hint sentence inside questAgentInstructionsFor (agent-instructions.ts line 59) -- the literal text written into every consumer's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md -- which predated QCLI-228 and never mentioned version-only. Fixed by adding an explicit carve-out: 'current instructions, and a version-only difference (only the pinned Quest CLI version number is stale) both exit 0; missing, drifted, or malformed managed instructions exit 6.' Regenerated this repo's own CLAUDE.md managed block from the corrected local source (bun run src/cli/main.ts agents --update-instructions --target claude) so tracker-integrity.yml continues to pass. Recorded DEC-4 documenting the decision (doc fix chosen over exit-code change; version-only stays 0 by design per QCLI-228, not reopened). Added a new test in test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts asserting the generated block text names the version-only exemption explicitly AND cross-checks that claim against checkQuestAgentInstructions's actual behavior for the same input. Manually verified --json and --plain render identical state/message for a version-only block in a throwaway workspace (both exit 0, state: version-only) -- structurally guaranteed by src/cli/main.ts's agents command sharing one instructionsResult computation for both output modes (only modeFor(parsed) differs).

Discovered scope beyond this task, reported rather than filed per instructions: quest decision create appears to have the same class of race QCLI-279 fixed for task ids. My first quest decision create call (against a branch cut from origin/dev before PR #79 landed) allocated id DEC-3 locally; origin/dev concurrently gained its own unrelated DEC-3 ('the joint quest/lore-cli projection+bound+omission shape', commit 9a57c4f, PR #79) via the same allocation path. Recovered by discarding the local .quest/planning.json diff, fast-forwarding the branch onto the new origin/dev tip, and re-running quest decision create, which correctly allocated DEC-4 against the now-current state. No .quest/ files were hand-edited. Not filing a follow-up task myself per this session's scope instructions -- reporting it back to the delegating session instead.
finalSummary: Root cause was narrower than the exit code: checkQuestBlockOnly already implemented QCLI-228's deliberate version-only=exit-0 design correctly, and guides.ts/command-help.ts already documented it correctly. Only the embedded CI-hint sentence inside questAgentInstructionsFor (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts) -- the literal text every quest agents --update-instructions writes into a consumer's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md -- predated QCLI-228 and never mentioned version-only, so it read as an unqualified exit-6 promise for all drift. Fixed the sentence to carve out version-only explicitly: 'current instructions, and a version-only difference (only the pinned Quest CLI version number is stale) both exit 0; missing, drifted, or malformed managed instructions exit 6.' Recorded DEC-4 stating the choice (documentation fix, not an exit-code change) and why. Regenerated this repo's own CLAUDE.md managed block from the corrected source so it dogfoods the fix and tracker-integrity.yml stays green. Added a test in test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts that pins the generated sentence's wording and cross-checks it against checkQuestAgentInstructions's actual version-only behavior for the same input, plus manually confirmed --json and --plain render identical state/message for a version-only block in a throwaway workspace. bun run check: 483 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. Discovered and reported (not filed, per scope) a decision-id allocation race in quest decision create, same class as QCLI-279's task-id bug -- hit and recovered from mid-task; details in implementation notes.
